messages.author: dd078ff33d6e1285
messages.subject: Random Effects Binomial GLM
parts:
Hello. Everyone. I am Sungwon Hong of Pusan National University in South Korea.

I am beginner, so I have problem. Please, help me.

I've submitted the paper, but the reviewer recommended to use the GLMM to address the spatial heterogeneity.

So I followed the chapter 5 of Fitting models using the bayesian modeling software in Applied hierarchical modeling in ecology.

I used the data of BOD, Stock, Pop in the same sites for 5 years related with otter occurrence in South Korea.

I would like to make the random effect with three variables. But my problem is to get answer " Dimension mismatch in subset expression of BOD".

Please, tell me how to deal with this problem.


y <- Occ
y[y > 0] <- 1 
BOD<-read.csv("BOD.csv")
Stock<-read.csv("Stock.csv")
Pop<-read.csv("Pop.csv")

# Bundle data
win.data <- list(y = y, M = nrow(y), J = ncol(y), BOD = BOD, Stock = Stock, Pop = Pop, BOD.Stock = BOD * Stock, Stock.Pop = Stock * Pop, BOD.Pop = BOD * Pop, BOD.Stock.Pop = BOD * Stock * Pop)
str(win.data)

# Specify model in BUGS language
cat(file = "RE.Bernoulli.txt", "
model {
    
# Priors
    mu.alpha0 <- logit(mean.theta)                  # Random intercepts
    mean.theta ~ dunif(0, 1)
    tau.alpha0 <- pow(sd.alpha0, -2)
    sd.alpha0 ~ dunif(0, 10)
    mu.alpha1 ~ dnorm(0, 0.001)                     # Random slope on BOD
    tau.alpha1 <- pow(sd.alpha1, -2)
    sd.alpha1 ~ dunif(0, 10)
    mu.alpha2 ~ dnorm(0, 0.001)                     # Random slope on Stock
    tau.alpha2 <- pow(sd.alpha2, -2)
    sd.alpha2 ~ dunif(0, 10)
    mu.alpha3 ~ dnorm(0, 0.001)                     # Random slope on Pop
    tau.alpha3 <- pow(sd.alpha3, -2)
    sd.alpha3 ~ dunif(0, 10)
    mu.alpha4 ~ dnorm(0, 0.001)                     # Random slope on BOD.Stock
    tau.alpha4 <- pow(sd.alpha4, -2)
    sd.alpha4 ~ dunif(0, 10)
    mu.alpha5 ~ dnorm(0, 0.001)                     # Random slope on Stock.Pop
    tau.alpha5 <- pow(sd.alpha5, -2)
    sd.alpha5 ~ dunif(0, 10)
    mu.alpha6 ~ dnorm(0, 0.001)                     # Random slope on BOD.Pop
    tau.alpha6 <- pow(sd.alpha6, -2)
    sd.alpha6 ~ dunif(0, 10)
    mu.alpha7 ~ dnorm(0, 0.001)                     # Random slope on BOD.Stock.Pop
    tau.alpha7 <- pow(sd.alpha7, -2)
    sd.alpha7 ~ dunif(0, 10)

# Likelihood
for (i in 1:M) {
  alpha0[i] ~ dnorm(mu.alpha0, tau.alpha0)        # Intercept random effects
  re00[i] <- alpha0[i] - mu.alpha0                 # same zero-centered
  alpha1[i] ~ dnorm(mu.alpha1, tau.alpha1)        # Intercept random effects
  re01[i] <- alpha1[i] - mu.alpha1                 # same zero-centered
  alpha2[i] ~ dnorm(mu.alpha2, tau.alpha2)        # Intercept random effects
  re02[i] <- alpha2[i] - mu.alpha2                 # same zero-centered
  alpha3[i] ~ dnorm(mu.alpha3, tau.alpha3)        # Intercept random effects
  re03[i] <- alpha3[i] - mu.alpha3                 # same zero-centered
  alpha4[i] ~ dnorm(mu.alpha4, tau.alpha4)        # Intercept random effects
  re04[i] <- alpha4[i] - mu.alpha4                 # same zero-centered
  alpha5[i] ~ dnorm(mu.alpha5, tau.alpha5)        # Intercept random effects
  re05[i] <- alpha5[i] - mu.alpha5                 # same zero-centered
  alpha6[i] ~ dnorm(mu.alpha6, tau.alpha6)        # Intercept random effects
  re06[i] <- alpha6[i] - mu.alpha6                 # same zero-centered
  alpha7[i] ~ dnorm(mu.alpha7, tau.alpha7)        # Intercept random effects
  re07[i] <- alpha7[i] - mu.alpha7                 # same zero-centered
  for (j in 1:J) {
    y[i, j] ~ dbern(theta[i, j])
    logit(theta[i, j]) <- alpha0[i] + alpha1[i] * BOD[i, j] + alpha2[i] * Stock[i, j] + alpha3[i] * Pop[i, j] + alpha4[i] * BOD.Stock[i, j] + alpha5[i] * Stock.Pop[i, j] + alpha6[i] * BOD.Pop[i, j] + alpha7[i] * BOD.Stock.Pop[i, j]
  }

# Covariate mean as a model for missing covariates
for (i in 1:M) {
  BOD[i] ~ dnorm(mu.BOD, tau.BOD) # Assume BOD normally distributed
}
mu.BOD ~ dnorm(0, 0.0001)
tau.BOD ~ pow(sd.BOD, -2)
sd.BOD ~ dunif(0, 100)
}
} ")

# Other model run preparations
inits <- function() list(alpha0 = rnorm(M), alpha1 = rnorm(M), alpha2 = rnorm(M), alpha3 = rnorm(M), alpha4 = rnorm(M), alpha5 = rnorm(M), alpha6 = rnorm(M), alpha7 = rnorm(M)) # Inits
params <- c("mu.alpha0", "sd.alpha0", "alpha0", "mu.alpha1", "sd.alpha1", "alpha1", "mu.alpha2", "sd.alpha2", "alpha2", "mu.alpha3", "sd.alpha3", "alpha3", "mu.alpha4", "sd.alpha4", "alpha4", "mu.alpha5", "sd.alpha5", "alpha5", "mu.alpha6", "sd.alpha6", "alpha6", "mu.alpha7", "sd.alpha7", "alpha7", "re00", "re01", "re02", "re03", "re04", "re05", "re06", "re07") # Params
ni <- 30000 ; nt <- 25 ; nb <- 5000 ; nc <- 3 # MCMC settings

# Call JAGS from R (ART 2.5min)
  out <- jags(win.data, inits, params, "RE.Bernoulli.txt", n.chains = nc, n.thin = nt, n.iter = ni, n.burnin= nb)
  
  par(mfrow = c(2, 2))
  
  traceplot(out, c("mu.alpha0", "sd.alpha0", "mu.alpha1", "sd.alpha1", "mu.alpha2", "sd.alpha2", "mu.alpha3", "sd.alpha3", "mu.alpha4", "sd.alpha4", "mu.alpha5", "sd.alpha5", "mu.alpha6", "sd.alpha6", "mu.alpha7", "sd.alpha7"))
  
  print(out, 3)

messages.subject: Re: Random Effects Binomial GLM
parts:
Hi Sungwon Hong,

I think issue is here

for (j in 1:J) {
    y[i, j] ~ dbern(theta[i, j])
    logit(theta[i, j]) <- alpha0[i] + alpha1[i] * BOD[i, j] + alpha2[i] * Stock[i, j] + alpha3[i] * Pop[i, j] + alpha4[i] * BOD.Stock[i, j] + alpha5[i] * Stock.Pop[i, j] + alpha6[i] * BOD.Pop[i, j] + alpha7[i] * BOD.Stock.Pop[i, j]
  }
# Covariate mean as a model for missing covariates
for (i in 1:M) {
  BOD[i] ~ dnorm(mu.BOD, tau.BOD) # Assume BOD normally distributed
}

Notice BOD is a matrix in the first logit-linear model and a vector down below. That is why it is telling you there is a dimension mismatch.

Cheers,

Adam
